feature: The nine forms of /GitPlan are chosen by one selecting option; help stops before any inspection and a wrong combination executes nothing

also: an option the form does not list

expected: The usage line and the argument hint list every option, and the nine forms are chosen by exactly one selecting option: --into, --status, --amend, --converge or --release.
The set name is [a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{0,23}, matched case-sensitively and never a Windows device name; --into names a local branch that is not main; --amend needs --expect-revision.

--help (and --lang) is handled first: the command shows its inline help and stops before any tool call, file read, skill load or repository inspection; a missing set name is asked for, and an unknown option, two selecting options or an option the form does not list is a usage error that executes nothing.
Without --apply (and without --release) the command only previews: nothing is registered, created or merged, nothing is fetched, and the only write is a scratch spec file outside every worktree.
The hosts spell the same forms (/GitPlan in Claude Code, /git-plan in Hermes, $git-plan in Codex) and the three READMEs show the same examples.

Every form that shows the plan prints the Requirements table and the Lanes table (with State and Head once the plan has state, and with the changes of every lane once a lane is integrated), rendered from the guard's result or from its record and never from memory; the inline help of the Claude Code command and of the Hermes and Codex adapters says so in every form.

contains: argument-hint: "<set> (--into <branch> | --status | --amend | --converge | --release) [--apply] [--create] [--expect-revision <n>] [--include-active] [--land] [--lang <language>] [--help]"
Handle `--help` first, even if other arguments are present.
Answer solely from the inline help below, then stop before any tool call, file read, skill load, or repository inspection.
If the set name is missing, show this help and ask for it before proceeding.
For an unknown option, or an option the form does not list, explain the error, show this help, and stop.
Usage: `/GitPlan <set> (--into <branch> | --status | --amend | --converge | --release) [--apply] [--create] [--expect-revision <n>] [--include-active] [--land] [--lang <language>] [--help]`

Forms (the selecting option `--into`, `--status`, `--amend`, `--converge` or `--release` chooses the form; two selecting options together, or an option the form does not list, is a usage error; `--lang <language>` and `--help` go with every form):

- `<set>`: Required (except with `--help`). Name of the plan: `[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{0,23}`, matched case-sensitively, and not a Windows device name (`con`, `nul`, `com1`, ...). It names the set record and the claims of its lanes.

- `--into <branch>`: Required to plan. Local branch the plan is made against and that `--land` later fast-forwards. Matched exactly (case-sensitive); it must not be `main`. The other forms read it from the set record.

- `--create`: With `--apply` of a plan or an amendment: also create the branches and worktrees of the registered lanes that do not exist yet. Without it the apply prints the `git worktree add` lines for you to run.
- `--status`: Read-only checklist: the sheet with the state of every lane and what remains.
- `--amend`: Re-plan a registered set. Needs `--expect-revision`.

- `--expect-revision <n>`: The record revision (a positive integer) the amendment, or with `--converge --apply` the previewed convergence, was made against; a record at another revision stops the command.

- `--include-active`: With `--converge`: treat a lane in state `active` that holds changes of its own against the current target as ready at its current tip, which the preview shows as its Head. In an apply this is your acceptance of those tips; a tip that moved since the preview stops the apply with a new preview.
- `--release`: Retire the set once its lanes are integrated: remove its claims and its record. The lane branches, their worktrees and the integration branch are not touched.

- `--lang <language>`: Language of the reply, as a name or code (for example `English`, `ja`); Chinese when absent. Command names, options, branch names, paths, SHAs, and status codes stay untranslated.

- `--apply`: With `--into`: register the plan the preview showed (the lane claims, the claim of the integration branch and the set record, written only through `magos_guard.py`). With `--amend`: register the amended plan. With `--converge`: merge the lanes into the integration branch. Without it, only a preview is shown.

- `--land`: With `--converge --apply`: after the merges and the checks, fast-forward `<branch>` to the integration branch with `git merge --ff-only`, only when `<branch>` still sits where the integration branch was cut from; otherwise it stops and says to rerun. It is refused, before any merge, while a lane is not ready or integrated (run without `--land` first).
- `--help`: Show this help and stop without inspecting or changing the repository.

- `/GitPlan <set> --into <branch>`: preview the plan: investigate Git and the code, write the requirements of the task, divide it into lanes with exclusive file ownership that are named after the topic of their change, prove it and print the Requirements table and the Lanes table (read-only).
- `/GitPlan <set> --into <branch> --apply`: register the plan the preview showed and print both tables from the record.
- `/GitPlan <set> --into <branch> --apply --create`: register it, also create the lane branches and worktrees, and print both tables from the record.

- `/GitPlan <set> --status`: both tables with the state and the head of every lane (once a lane is integrated, also what it changed: the Changes column, the Result column and the Changes summary) and what remains (read-only).
- `/GitPlan <set> --amend --expect-revision <n>`: preview the re-plan of a registered set with both tables (read-only).
- `/GitPlan <set> --amend --expect-revision <n> --apply [--create]`: register the amended plan and print both tables from the record.
- `/GitPlan <set> --converge [--include-active]`: preview the convergence: both tables with the state of every lane, the merge plan and what remains (read-only).

- `/GitPlan <set> --converge --apply [--include-active] [--land] [--expect-revision <n>]`: merge the lanes into the integration branch and print the original tables supplemented with the changes of every lane (Changes, Result, the Changes summary and its Total line); `--land` also fast-forwards `<branch>`.
- `/GitPlan <set> --release`: print the supplemented tables, then retire the set after its lanes are integrated.

Examples: `/GitPlan sweep-readiness --into develop`, `/GitPlan sweep-readiness --into develop --apply --create`, `/GitPlan sweep-readiness --status`, `/GitPlan sweep-readiness --converge --apply --land`, `/GitPlan --help`.

- Default: Investigate Git and the code, then print the plan preview: the Requirements table (each requirement of the task with the lanes that serve it and their planned outcomes), the Lanes table (branch, worktree, owned paths, dependencies, acceptance), the merge line, the shared files and the risks, the topic each lane id names, the proof that the lane manifests are pairwise disjoint (`magos_guard.py set-plan --dry-run`) and a readiness verdict (`READY` or `BLOCKED`) with the next command and the remedy for every failed gate; nothing is registered, created or merged, nothing is fetched, and the only write is a scratch spec file outside every worktree.
